Subject: Contract term amendment & increased throughput request

Hi Jordan,

Quick note from the ops side here — we had a bigger-than-expected rollout for a new feature in late Aug and our token consumption spiked ~3.2x in Q3. The attached Q3 export shows the daily token burn (summary attached). Based on forecasted demand from two additional product teams, we expect steady usage of ~250M tokens/month starting Nov.

Current contract has us at a 60M token commit/month with monthly overage billing. Procurement would like to discuss:
- Amending the term to add a 12-month extension starting Nov 1
- Increasing committed tokens to 250M / month (or equivalent reserved throughput)
- Prefer a committed pricing model rather than high overage exposure

Can you send a short ROI recap (cost vs current spend) and a draft amendment the legal team can review? Procurement (cc'd if needed) will want to know proration and effective date.

Thanks — attaching the usage CSV for context.

Attachments: HexaTek_Q3_usage_report.csv (CSV)

Best,

1) Pricing: I recommend we present two options to HexaTek — (A) 12-month committed 250M/month with 18% discount (preferred), (B) 6-month bridge at 200M/month with 12% discount and option to convert mid-term. That gives procurement flexibility.

Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed amendment + ROI snapshot for HexaTek (options A/B)

Priya — attaching a short amendment and a one-page ROI summary for procurement. Apologies for the multiple docs — wanted to give a clear A/B option set. Summary below:

Option A (Recommended) — 12 months
- Commit: 250M tokens / month
- Effective: Nov 1, 2026 (12-month extension)
- Unit economics: $0.60 per 1k tokens on committed units (18% off list)
- Estimated monthly cost: ~$150,000 (estimated based on current usage forecast)
- Expected savings vs current overage path: ~28% on token spend vs projected demand
- SLA & perf: 95th percentile generation latency < 150ms across our hosted regions; auto-fallback to equivalent model variant if capacity constrained

Option B — 6-month bridge (convertible)
- Commit: 200M tokens / month
- Discount: 12% off list
- Allows conversion to Option A mid-term if usage stabilizes

Billing/proration note: If signed by Oct 15 we can align the first committed invoice to Nov 1 and credit any overages billed in Oct up to the committed delta (Sales Ops to confirm exact credit amounts). Doc attached has the proration examples.

Attachments: HexaTek_Amendment_v1.pdf (PDF), pricing_sheet_oct2026.xlsx (Excel)

If this looks good, I can route the amendment to your legal/procurement and send via DocuSign for signature. Would you prefer Option A or should we present both to Procurement?

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks for the fast turnaround and clear options. Procurement is looped (cc'd above). We like Option A in principle; main questions before we sign:

1) Final proration mechanics — if we sign on Oct 20, will Oct usage be credited toward the Nov commitment or will we receive a one-time credit?
2) Can you confirm whether the committed units are bill-in-advance or billed monthly post-usage? We prefer billed monthly in arrears if possible.
3) Any limitations on model upgrades during the committed term (we want to ensure we can adopt model improvements without being forced into a higher price tier).

If you can answer 1–3 and send the DocuSign link I can get this through procurement next week.

Best,
Priya
Director of Platform Ops, HexaTek

Subject: Re: Proposed amendment + ROI snapshot for HexaTek (options A/B) — answers + DocuSign

Priya / Carlos — quick responses inline: 

1) Proration: If signed on Oct 20 we will credit Oct overages against the Nov commitment up to the committed delta. Sales Ops (Marcus) has generated three sign-date scenarios and the numbers are in the attached pricing sheet; I'll summarize in the DocuSign cover note.
2) Billing cadence: We can support monthly billing in arrears for committed units (invoice at month-end for prior month consumption against the commit). We'll add the billing cadence clause to the amendment.
3) Model upgrades: No forced upgrades. The amendment will include a clause that allows access to backward-compatible model improvements; major architecture/variant upgrades that materially change cost will be agreed via a notification and 30-day discussion window before being enforced.

I've attached the final amendment (updated with billing cadence and proration language) and just sent it via DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/00A1B2C3. Please route to Procurement and Legal; happy to hop on a call if helpful.

Attachments: HexaTek_Amendment_v1.pdf (PDF), pricing_sheet_oct2026.xlsx (Excel)

Thanks all — Jordan
